fields.v: Table 1 columns jumbled in pdftotext; mapping reconstructed and checked against text deltas (5.4/5.3/3.8 points, +$0.01-0.03). Possible inconsistency: text says CodeSpec achieves 'the highest number of resolved tasks' on Fast and Full, but mapped Table 1 gives Mini-SWE-Agent 24 vs CodeSpec 17 on Fast. The ablation 'w/o All Specification' (Table 3: 62.6±6.0, 7, $0.09) is identical to Mini-SWE-Agent on Lite (Table 1), suggesting CodeSpec runs on Mini-SWE-Agent, which the paper does not state. Claude Code and other baselines run with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, not their native models. Abstract's '70.7%, 55.0%, 49.9% pass rates' are %Passed (share of tests), not resolve rate. Figure 3 values jumbled; text values used. Interaction budget K and prompts not given. Code and data: github.com/zhu-zhu-ding/CodeSpec. Pre-registration: not claimed. Language: Python
fields.quote: Removing all specifications decreases %Passed from 70.7% to 62.6% and reduces the number of resolved tasks from 9 to 7
fields.where: RQ2: Ablation Study, Table 3, p. 6 (vs Table 1, p. 5)
fields.why: The 'w/o All Specification' ablation reproduces the Mini-SWE-Agent Lite row exactly (62.6, 7, $0.09), an unreported link that bears on what CodeSpec's gain is measured against.
fields.doubt: A linha 'w/o All Specification' da Tabela 3 (62.6, 7, 0.09 $) é igual à do Mini-SWE-Agent no Lite (Tabela 1). Parece que o CodeSpec corre sobre o Mini-SWE-Agent, o que o artigo não diz. Vê as págs. 5-6 e decide se o acrescentas às Notas.
